§ 419. Filing of Notice of Pendency and Effect Thereof. 

The filing of the notice of pendency serves as constructive notice from the time of such filing, to a purchaser or encumbrancer of the property affected thereby, from or against a defendant with respect to whom the notice is directed to be indexed. C.P.A., § 121. Mentz v. Efficient Building Corp. et al., 145 Misc. 505, 261 

N. Y. S. 242. In Kestler v. Weissenfels et al., 247 A. D. 

888, 286 N. Y. S. 790, an action was brought to impress upon certain realty a lien of $3300, paid by the plaintiff to the seller. The plaintiff filed the lis pendens and verified complaint on June 24, 1933, at 10:34 A.M.; seventeen minutes later, the defendants who took title to the property from the seller, who was obligated to repay the plaintiff $3300, recorded their deed. The court affirmed the judgment in favor of the plaintiff, holding that the plaintiff's rights under a lis pendens are superior to those arising under an unrecorded deed. The court further held that the principle underlying the doctrine of lis pendens does not rest upon the presumption of notice, but upon reasons of public policy, citing Kursheedt v. Union Dime Sav. Institution, 118 N. Y. 358;

Ayrault v. Murphy, 54 N. Y. 203; People's Trust Co. v. 

Tonkonogy, 144 A. D. 333, 128 N. Y. S. 1055.

A person whose conveyance or incumbrance is sub-

419 

413 sequently executed or recorded is bound by all the proceedings taken in the action after the filing of the notice, to the same extent as if he were a party to the action. C.P.A., § 121. The notice is filed with the verified complaint, as a rule, before the service of the summons. But, in any event, the plaintiff must file the notice of pendency in the clerk's office of each county where the mortgaged property is situated, at least twenty days before the final judgment directing a sale is rendered. C.P.A., § 1080. The filing of such notice is an indispensable prerequisite to the entry of a judgment.. 

Beck v. Williams, 116 Misc. 80, 190 N. Y. S. 256, citing

Wait's N. Y. Practice [2nd Ed.] § 621. Rule 258 of the 

Rules of Civil Practice provides that when the plaintiff moves for judgment, he must show by affidavit, or by the certificate of the clerk of the county wherein the mortgaged premises are situated that the notice has been filed at least twenty days before such application for judgment and at or after the time of filing the complaint. 

The notice is required to be filed with the verified complaint in order to be effective and thus care should be taken to see that the complaint is properly verified.. 

In Beck v. Williams, 116 Misc. 80, 190 N. Y. S. 256, the lis pendens was filed twenty days before the judgment as required, but the record showed that the complaint had been verified one year before the action accrued. 

The court held that a verified complaint meant a properly verified complaint and because the verification was defective, it was not a verified complaint within the meaning of the statute so as to entitle the plaintiff to file the lis pendens.

Where the notice is filed with the complaint before the service of the summons, personal or substituted service of the summons must be made upon a defendant, within sixty days after the filing, or else, before the expiration of the same time, publication of the summons:

$ 421 

must be commenced, or service thereof must be made without the state, as prescribed by law. C.P.A., § 120. 

A defendant may file a like notice of pendency at the time of filing his answer or at any time afterwards before final judgment where he sets up in his answer a counterclaim upon which he demands an affirmative judgment affecting the title to, or the possession, use or enjoyment of real property. C.P.A., § 125. Farbro Corp. v. 

A. F. A. Realty Corp. et al., 261 N. Y. 24. 

§ 420. Recording and Indexing of Notice of Pendency. 

Each county clerk with whom a notice of pendency is filed must immediately record it in a book kept in his office for that purpose and index it in the name of each defendant, specified in the direction appended at the foot of the notice. C.P.A., § 122. 

§ 421. Cancellation of Lis Pendens. 

C.P.A., § 123 provides that after the action is settled, discontinued or abated, or final judgment is rendered therein against the party filing the notice, and the time to appeal therefrom has expired, or if a plaintiff filing the notice unreasonably neglects to proceed in the action, the court, in its discretion, upon the application of any person aggrieved and upon such notice as may be directed or approved by it, may direct that a notice of the pendency of an action be cancelled of record by a particular clerk, or by all the clerks, with whom it is filed and recorded. The cancellation must be made by a note to that effect on the margin of the record, referring to the order. Unless the order is entered in the same clerk's office, a certified copy thereof must be filed therein before the notice is cancelled.

After the notice has been cancelled, neither the proceedings in the action nor any judgment which may be rendered therein will affect the real property described

423 415 

in the cancelled notice. C.P.A., § 121; Valentine v. 

Austin, 124 N. Y. 400, aff'g 58 Hun 398, 12 N. Y. S. 196. 

§ 422. Notice of Object of Action and of No Personal 

Claim.

In as much as certain persons are made parties in a foreclosure action in order to extinguish any interest or lien they may have, but no personal claim is asserted against them, a notice to this effect is prepared and served upon them with the summons. A defendant is thus notified that no claim is made against him personally and hence no need to interpose an answer. But if, under the circumstances, the defendant unreasonably defends, he is penalized to the extent of having costs awarded against him. C.P.A., § 1478; Bidwell v. Sullivan, 17 A. D. 

629, 45 N. Y. S. 530; West End Sav. & L. Ass'n v. Degan, 4 A. D. 618, 39 N. Y. S. 414.

The notice sets forth the general object of the action, a brief description of the property affected by it, if it affects specific real or personal property and that a personal claim is not made against the defendant. See form, § 50. 

§ 423. Preparation of Complaint-Form. 

Venue-As already stated, the action is brought in the supreme court in the county where the property or some part thereof is situated. It may also be brought in the county court where the property to which the action relates is situated within the county. 

Parties-All the owners of a mortgage; that is, the mortgagees, including the personal representatives of any deceased mortgagee, should be united as plaintiffs in an action to foreclose, except that one whose consent cannot be obtained, may be made a defendant, the complaint stating the reason therefor. Dahl v. Levenberg, 172 A. D. 919, 157 N. Y. S. 14. See Wait's N. Y. Practice

Vol. 5. [4th Ed.] 189-194. 27

§ 423 

With respect to the commencement of an action by the owner of a junior participating interest in a mortgage, C.P.A., § 1079-a provides that an action may be maintained by the owner of a junior participating share or interest in a bond secured by a mortgage on real, or on real and personal property, for the payment of principal and/or interest and/or for foreclosure of such bond and mortgage, in its entirety, or in the alternative, subject to the interest of the owner of the senior share notwithstanding that the entire mortgage debt may be due and payable, in the event that the owner of the senior share to whom is given the right in the participating agreement to enforce such bond and mortgage shall fail or refuse to commence an action for the enforcement of such bond and/or mortgage, after ten days' written notice and demand to commence any such action, following default in the performance of any of the terms and covenants thereof. Upon such failure or refusal, the junior participant may exercise any and all options and remedies provided in such bond and mortgage or otherwise available to any holder thereof. This section was made applicable to pending actions, providing written notice of default was given and demand made as provided in this section. 

To determine who the defendants shall be, it is necessary to have in mind the purpose of a foreclosure action; to wit, to bar all persons and foreclose and extinguish any right, title and equity of redemption which they may have in and to the mortgaged premises by reason of liens acquired subsequent to the execution of the mortgage. One should first of all obtain the name of the owner of the premises; for the owner of the equity of redemption is a necessary party. If he is not served, the purchaser at the sale, derives no title whatsoever. 

Hermann v. Cabinet Land Co., 217 N. Y. 526. The next step is to ascertain the identity of all other lienors by searching all conveyances and liens arising subsequent

§ 417 

to the date of the mortgage. A search of this sort may be arranged for through a title company. The names of all tenants and other persons in possession should be ascertained since the occupant or person in possession of the premises at the time of the commencement of the foreclosure action is an indispensable party no matter how or under what circumstances he came into possession. Scheidt v. Supreme Woodworking Co., Inc., 212 

A. D. 179, 208 N. Y. S. 394. A tenant not made a party is not bound by the decree, and if omitted, he cannot be ejected until the expiration of his tenancy. In Heller v. Cohen, 154 N. Y. 299, where the occupant was not made a party, the court held that because the purchasers at the sale could not obtain possession except by means of an action brought for the purpose of determining that the occupant had no right, title or interest in the premises, the title was not one which the purchasers would be obliged to accept. Timmerman v. Cohn, 204 

N. Y. 614. Prior incumbrancers need not be made parties. 

Clark v. Fuller, 136 Misc. 151, 239 N. Y. S. 269. They may, however, be made parties to have the amount due them, liquidated. 

C.P.A., § 1079 provides that each of the following persons whose interest is claimed to be subject and subordinate to the plaintiff's lien, must be made a party defendant in an action to foreclose: "1. Every person having an estate or interest in possession, or otherwise, in the property as tenant in fee, for life, by the curtesy, or for years. 

2. Every person entitled to the reversion, remainder, or inheritance of the real property, or of any interest therein or undivided share thereof, after the determination of a particular estate therein. 

3. Every person who by any contingency contained in a devise or grant or otherwise is or may become entitled to a beneficial interest in the property or an undivided

8 423 

share thereof, or in the proceeds of sale thereof, provided that where a future estate or interest is limited in any contingency to the persons who shall compose a certain class upon the happening of a future event, it shall be sufficient to make parties to the action all persons who would have been entitled to such estate or interest or proceeds of sale, if such event had happened immediately before the commencement of the action. 

4. Every person having an inchoate right of dower in the real property or any part or share thereof. 

5. Every person having a right of dower in the property or any part or share thereof. 

6. Every person having any lien or incumbrance upon the real property which is claimed to be subject and subordinate to the lien of the plaintiff. 

7. Any person who is liable to the plaintiff for payment of the debt secured by the mortgage may be made a defendant in the action. The people of the State of New 

York may be made a party defendant to an action for the foreclosure of a mortgage on real property, where the people of the State of New York have an interest in or a lien on the said real property subsequent to the lien of the mortgage sought to be foreclosed in said action, in the same manner as a private person. In an action to foreclose a mortgage upon any of the public utilities regulated by the public service commissions law, the public service commission having supervision thereof shall be made a party defendant. Service of summons upon any such commission shall be made by delivering a copy thereof within the state to a commissioner, a deputy commissioner or the secretary of the commission. 

Subd. 2. In all cases where prior to September first, nineteen hundred and thirty-six, a judgment has been entered in an action for the foreclosure of a mortgage, and to such action there have been made parties defendant all persons who would have been entitled to an estate

423 419 

or interest in the property, or in the proceeds of sale thereof upon the happening of a future event if such event had happened immediately before the commencement of said action, such judgment shall be deemed binding and conclusive upon every other person who may or might have such estate or interest unless such other person not a party to said action shall within one year after this act takes effect bring an action to redeem said real property from said mortgage pursuant to section fortysix of this act, and a notice of pendency of such action be duly filed."

Where parties are unknown, they should be designated as such as provided in C.P.A., § 215. If there are infants, application should be made for the appointment of a guardian ad litem. 

Allegations-The complaint should set out the indebtedness clearly. Troy City Bank v. Bowman, 43 Barb. 

639. In that case it was held that where the complaint set out the indebtedness of the mortgagors upon notes indorsed by them and discounted by the plaintiff, and alleged that the mortgage was given to secure the payment of a bond by which the time for the payment of such indebtedness was considerably extended; and that the obligors had failed to comply with the conditions of the bond; these facts constituted a sufficient cause of action. It should allege non-payment of the debt secured by the mortgage or other breach of condition according to the circumstances. Sun, etc. Bldg. Assoc. v. Buck, 36 A. D. 637, 55 N. Y. S. 262. Where the right to foreclose depends on title to the bond, it is not sufficient to allege the assignment of the mortgage and not that of the bond it was given to secure. Manne v. Carlson, 49 

A. D. 276, 63 N. Y. S. 162; Smith v. Thompson, 118 A. D. 

6, 103 N. Y. S. 336. The complaint should state whether any other action has been brought to recover any part of the mortgage debt, and if so, whether any part thereof has been collected. Rule 255; Dahl v. Levenberg, 172

$ 423 

A. D. 919, 157 N. Y. S. 14; Schieck v. Donohue, 77 A. D. 

321, 79 N. Y. S. 233, appeal dismissed 173 N. Y. 638;

Lovett v. German Reformed Church, 12 Barb. 67. The prayer for relief will demand judgment that the defendants and all persons claiming under them subsequent to the commencement of the action may be forever barred and foreclosed of and from any right, title, claim, lien and equity of redemption in the mortgaged premises or any part thereof; that the premises may be decreed to be sold, and that the proceeds arising from the sale may be paid in satisfaction of the mortgage indebtedness, costs and expenses of the action and of the sale, and that the defendants who are liable, may be adjudged to pay any deficiency which may remain after applying all moneys applicable thereto. Termansen v. Matthews, 49 A. D. 163, 63 N. Y. S. 115; Leopold v. Epstein, 54 A. D. 

133, 66 N. Y. S. 414; Bernard v. Onderdonk, 98 N. Y. 

167; See Wait's N. Y. Practice Vol. 5 [4th Ed.] 195–201.

The complaint may be in the following form:

§ 424. Service of Summons and Complaint. 

The summons and complaint are served as in other civil actions. Care, however, should be taken to specially note those provisions of the Civil Practice Act, which relate to the service of such parties as infants, incompetents, absentees, etc. The action is commenced by the service of the summons and not by the filing of the lis pendens. Mentz v. Efficient Building Corp. et al., 145 

Misc. 505, 261 N. Y. S. 242.

As has already been stated, if the notice of pendency has been filed before the service of the summons, personal or substituted service of the summons must be made upon the defendant, within sixty days after the filing or else before the expiration of the same time, publication of the summons is commenced or service thereof must be made without the state as prescribed by law. C.P.A., § 120. The summons may be served with the verified complaint, and, in the case of defendants against whom no personal claim is asserted, the summons is served with notice of object and of no personal claim. 

§ 425. Proof of Service and Filing Thereof-Form. 

After service of the summons has been effected, an

8. 427 

affidavit of service is prepared. Rule 53. In may be filed with the clerk of the court with whom the summons, verified complaint and lis pendens were filed. 

The affidavit of service may read as follows: 

-against- Plaintiff,

GEORGE CASE and MARY CASE, his wife, MAY HAMPTON and ROBERT SMITH, Defendants.

JACK FARR, being duly sworn, deposes and says that he is over the age of twenty-one years, and resides at No. 1709 East 

2nd Street, Borough of Brooklyn, City of New York.

That on the 27th day of July, 1933, your deponent served the summons and complaint in this action on George Case and Mary Case, two of the defendants in this action at No. 19 Row 8th 

Street, Borough of Brooklyn, City of New York, by delivering a copy of said summons and verified complaint to and leaving the same with each of said defendants personally. That your deponent further says he knew the persons so served and knew them to be the persons mentioned in said summons and complaint as two of the defendants herein.

Your deponent further served the summons together with a notice of object of action and of no personal claim in the above entitled action upon Robert Smith and May Hampton, two of the defendants therein named, at No. 19 Row 8th Street, Brooklyn, City of New York on the 31st day of July, 1933, by delivering a copy of said summons and notice of object of action and of no personal claim to, and leaving the same with each of said defendants personally. That your deponent further says he knew the persons so served and knew them to be the persons

$ 428 

mentioned and described in said summons and notice of object of action and of no personal claim as two of the defendants in this action. 

2nd day of August, 1933.

RICHARD BOYD, Notary Public-Kings County. 

§ 426. Dismissal of Complaint. 

JOHN FARR. 

C.P.A., § 1081 provides that where an action is brought to foreclose a mortgage upon real property upon which a portion of the principal or interest is due, and another portion of either is to become due, the complaint must be dismissed, without costs against the plaintiff, upon the defendant paying into court, at any time before a final judgment directing a sale is rendered, the sum due and the plaintiff's costs. Trowbridge v. Malex R. Corp., 198 A. D. 656, 191 N. Y. S. 97. 

§ 427. Answer. 

An answer may be interposed in the same manner as in other civil actions unless a notice of object and of no personal claim has been served. The answer is in the usual form and may contain the usual defenses such as fraud, payment, usury, statute of limitations, etc. It may also contain counterclaims. See Wait's N. Y.

Practice Vol. V. [4th Ed.] page 201. And where no issue is intended to be raised, a guardian ad litem may, nevertheless, interpose a general answer on behalf of the infant. Rule 256. See form Bradbury's Lawyer's

Manual [4th Ed.] page 1044. 

§ 428. Notice of Appearance and Waiver-Form. 

Where a defendant is served and does not intend to interpose an answer, he may, nevertheless, serve a notice of appearance in order that he may receive notice of all subsequent proceedings; for where a party appears,

428 429 

he is entitled to notice of every proceeding therein which may affect him injuriously except in those cases where by the rules and practice of the court, he is bound to watch the proceedings, so as to protect his rights without such notice. Mahnk v. Blanchard, 233 A. D. 

555, 253 N. Y. S. 307, citing Knapp v. Burnham, 11

Paige Ch. 330. In a foreclosure action, under such circumstances, it is customary to serve a notice of appearance and waiver of the service of all papers and of notices of all proceedings except notice of sale, and of proceedings to obtain surplus moneys. 

The notice of appearance and waiver reads as follows: 

SUPREME COURT-Albany County. 

DOE COMPANY, Plaintiff, -against- 

RICHARD ROE, MARY SMITH AND FRANK BOYD, Defendants. 

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that the defendant Mary Smith, hereby appears in the above entitled action and that we are hereby retained by and appear as attorneys for her therein, and do hereby waive service of all papers and notices of all proceedings in said action, except notice of sale, and of proceedings to obtain surplus moneys.

Dated: New York, January 3, 1935. 

Yours, etc.,

JONES & SMITH, 

Attorneys for Defendant, Mary Smith.

Office and Post Office Address, 

165 Broadway,

Borough of Manhattan, City of New York.

$ 430 

To: 

DAVIS & HARRIS, ESQS., 

Attorneys for Plaintiff. 

120 Broadway,

§ 429. Procedure Following Service of Answer or of Notice of Appearance. 

If an answer is interposed, the action proceeds to trial in the manner of other equity actions. See local court rules entitling the action to a preference. Supreme 

Ct. N. Y. Cty. Spec. Term Rule IX, subd. 2; Kings Cty.

Supreme Ct. Spec. Term Rule 22; Bronx Cty. Supreme Ct. Rule IV, subd. 2. 

Where no answer is interposed but a notice of appearance and waiver only, is served, and the court does not compute the amount due, application may be made for the appointment of a referee to compute. 

§ 430. Application for Reference to Compute-Default Action. 

Rule 256 of the Rules of Civil Practice, provides as 

"Reference on default or admission. If, in an action to foreclose a mortgage, the defendant fail to answer within the time allowed for that purpose, or the right of the plaintff, as stated in the complaint, is admitted by the answer, unless the court shall ascertain and determine the amount due, the plaintiff may have an order referring it to some suitable person as referee to compute the amount due to the plaintiff and to such of the defendants as are prior encumbrancers of the mortgaged premises, and to examine and report whether the mortgaged premises can be sold in parcels, and, if the whole amount secured by the mortgage has not become due, he shall report the amount thereafter to become due. 

Where the defendant is an infant, and has put in a general answer by his guardian, or if any of the defendants be absentees, the order of reference also shall direct

§ 431 

the person to whom it is referred to take proof of the facts and circumstances stated in the complaint and to examine the plaintiff or his agent, on oath, as to any payments which have been made, and to compute the amount due on the mortgage, preparatory to the application for judgment of foreclosure and sale." 

The appointment of a referee to compute is not obligatory in a case where there is a default or a general answer by an infant's guardian ad litem; for the computation may be made by the court. DeGroot v. Morwick Const. 

Co., 98 Misc. 374, 163 N. Y. S. 83. But although the court may compute, it is customary to refer the matter to a referee and thus save the time of the courts. This is especially true in those courts which have congested calendars.

It is to be noted that unless the court directs otherwise, a reference is to be had in the county wherein the action is triable. Rule 191. And thus, where the venue of an action was laid in Queens County and the reference to compute was noticed for and had in New York County, the referee's report was vacated. Beach Seventieth St. 

Holding Corp. v. Beachland, Inc., 161 Misc. 445, 291 N. 

Y. S. 262.

§ 433. Procedure Following Preparation of Motion Papers to Compute. 

The motion papers for a reference to compute are served upon the attorneys for the parties who have appeared and not waived. They are filed with the affidavit or admission of service with the clerk in special term in the part wherein the motion is made returnable in advance of the return day except in those courts where a note of issue is required to be filed to place the motion on the calendar. 

§ 434. Order of Reference to Compute-Form. 

An order to be entered on the motion for a reference to compute may be prepared and submitted on the return day of the motion. It is in the usual form and provides, among other things that upon the coming in and filing of the referee's report, it be confirmed as of course. A blank space is left for the court to insert the name of the referee.

The order may read as follows: 

PRESENT: 

At a Special Term, Part I, of the Supreme 

Court of the State of New York, held in and for the County of Kings, at the 

County Courthouse in the Borough of 

Brooklyn, City and State of New York, on the 17th day of October, 1933.

HON. THOMAS J. CUFF, Justice.

 Plaintiff, -against- 

GEORGE CASE and MARY CASE, his wife, MAY HAMPTON and ROBERT SMITH, Defendants.

§ 435. Service of Order With Notice of Entry. 

The order of reference with notice of entry may be served upon the attorneys for the parties who have appeared and not waived. A certified copy thereof with notice of entry is served upon the referee, and a date is arranged for the hearing. 

§ 436. The Referee. 

Rule 265 of the Rules of Civil Practice provides that the referee to be appointed in foreclosure actions to

§ 437 

compute the amount due shall be selected by the court, and the court shall not appoint as such referee a person nominated by a party to the action or his counsel. His qualifications are set forth in Rule 172. 

§ 437. Referee's Summons-Form. 

A referee's summons may, when necessary, be prepared by the plaintiff's attorney, signed by the referee, and served on the attorneys. The court in Beach Seventieth St. Holding Corp. v. Beachland, Inc., 161 Misc. 445, 291 N. Y. S. 262 stated that it knew of no statute which prescribes the length of the notice that should be given of the hearing before a referee to compute. Such a notice is not a notice of motion and is not governed by the rules relating to motions. Irrespective of the defendant's general appearance, it might have required a five days' notice of the hearing by serving the notice specified in subdivision 2 of Rule 190. Not having done so, the court held three days' notice was sufficient. 

In a case where there are absentee or infant defendants, and the referee is required to take proof of matters pursuant to Rule 256, the referee's summons may read as follows: 

DOE COMPANY, 

-against- Plaintiff,

RICHARD ROE, MARY SMITH and FRANK BOYD, Defendants. 

By virtue of an order made by Honorable Thomas J. Cuff, one of the Justices of this Court, and entered herein on the 

10th day of January, 1936, I, John Doe, the Referee appointed

438 439 

therein, do hereby summon you to appear at my office, No. 120 

Broadway, in the Borough of Manhattan in the City of New 

York, on the 20th day of January, 1936, at 10 o'clock in the forenoon to attend a hearing of the matters in said action in reference before me as such Referee pursuant to said order. 

And hereof fail not at your peril.

Dated: New York, January 11, 1936. 

To: 

JOHN DOE, Referee. 

(Names of attorneys.) UNDERWRITING. 

To take proof of the facts and circumstances stated in the complaint and to examine the plaintiff or its agent on oath as to any payments which have been made and to ascertain and compute the amount due to the plaintiff on the bond and mortgage set forth in the complaint, and to examine and report whether the mortgaged premises can be sold in parcels. 

§ 438. Hearing Before Referee. 

JOHN DOE, Referee.

Before proceeding to hear the testimony, the referee is first sworn faithfully and fairly to try the issues, or to determine the question referred to him, as the case requires, and to make a just and true report according to the best of his understanding. The referee's oath may be waived if all the parties whose interest will be affected by the result are of age and present in person or by attorney. C.P.R. 171. Upon the hearing and for the convenience of the referee, the plaintiff's attorney may produce an itemized statement of the various amounts as computed by him. He should also produce such documentary evidence as the case requires, such as the bond, mortgage, assignment of mortgage, extension agreements, if any; receipted bills for payments made by the mortgagee, such as those for taxes, assessments, water rates, penalties or interest and insurance

8 439 

premiums. The referee's fee is twenty-five dollars for which a receipt should be obtained to be annexed to the report. C.P.A., § 1545. 

Where there are infant or absentee defendants, and the order directs that the referee take proof of the facts and circumstancs stated in the complaint, and to examine the plaintiff or his agent, on oath, as to any payments which have been made, and to compute the amount due, a record of the hearing is made showing appearances, testimony, etc. See form in Bradbury's 

Lawyer's Manual [4th Ed.] page 1094. If no such record is required to be made, the report will be in the form as hereinafter described. 

§ 439. Referee's Oath-Form. 

Where the papers are silent as to whether the referee took the oath, the presumption is in favor of the performance of his official duty. Hatfield v. Malcolm, 71 

Hun 51, 24 N. Y. S. 596. The oath is prepared pursuant to Rule 171 to read as follows:

-against- Plaintiff,

GEORGE CASE and MARY CASE, his wife, MAY HAMPTON and ROBERT SMITH, Defendants. 

SS.: 

EDWARD A. JONES, Referee, appointed by an order of this 

Court in the above entitled action dated the 17th day of October, 1933, to ascertain and compute the amount due to the plaintiff upon the bond and mortgage mentioned in the complaint herein, and to examine and report whether the mortgaged

8.441 

premises can be sold in parcels, being duly sworn, deposes and says:

That I will faithfully determine herein the matters referred to me, as the said order requires me to do, in the said action, and that I will make a just and true report thereon according to the best of my understanding. 

 23rd day of November, 1933.

MARY SMITH, Notary Public-Kings County. 

EDWARD A. JONES. 

§ 440. Referee's Report on Reference to Compute-Form. 

Where there are no infant or absentee defendants, the referee's report on a reference to compute may be in 

-against- Plaintiff,

I, EDWARD A. JONES, Referee in said order named, do report 

---

8 440 

1. That before proceeding to hear the testimony or to act as such Referee I was first duly sworn faithfully and fairly to hear and determine the matters referred to me as required by said order in this action, and to make a just and true report thereon according to the best of my understanding. 

2. That I have taken proof of the facts and circumstances stated in the complaint herein and have examined the plaintiff on oath, and find that the facts and circumstances stated in the complaint and all the material allegations thereof are true. 

3. February, 1933, amounting to $393.75, together with a semiannual instalment of interest due and payable on the 1st day of February, 1933, amounting to $225, and taxes, assessments and water charges aggregating $435.43, with accrued interest amounting to $15.99, making a total due and payable on the plaintiff's bond and mortgage in the sum of Eight thousand five hundred seventy and 17/100 ($8,570.17) Dollars.

§ 441. Filing Report of Reference. 

The report on the reference to compute is signed by the referee and filed as provided in the order of reference, preparatory to the application for judgment of foreclosure. 

§ 442. Notice of Filing of Referee's Report and of Application to Confirm and for Judgment of Foreclosure and Sale-Form. 

After the referee's report has been filed, a notice of filing is served upon the attorneys for the parties who have appeared and not waived. The notice of filing may be combined with a notice of motion to confirm the referee's report and for application for judgment of foreclosure with costs and for an extra allowance in addition to costs pursuant to C.P.A., § 1513. 

The parties who have appeared and defaulted in pleading are entitled to five days' notice of application for judgment. Rule 190, subd. 1.

§ 443. Affidavit of Regularity in Support of Application for Judgment of Foreclosure and Sale-Form. 

An affidavit in support of an application for judgment of foreclosure, must show, among other things, whether any of the defendants who have not appeared are absentees, and if any of the defendants who have not appeared are absentees or if any of the defendants are infants, the plaintiff must, if the court has not computed, produce the referee's report of the examination of the plaintiff or his agent, on oath as to any payments which have been made and as to proof of the facts and circumstances stated in the complaint. Rule 257. It must also be shown either by the affidavit or the certificate of the clerk of the county in which the mortgaged premises are situated that a notice of pendency of the action containing the names of the parties thereto; the object of the action; a description of the property; the date of the mortgage, the parties thereto, and the time and place of recording the same, has been filed at least twenty days before such application for judgment and at or after the time of filing the complaint as required by law. 

Rule 258.

§ 445. Judgment of Foreclosure and Sale-Form. 

Rule 259 provides that every judgment for the sale of mortgaged premises shall contain the description and particular boundaries of the property to be sold; that unless otherwise specially ordered by the court, the judgment shall direct that the premises, or so much thereof as may be sufficient to discharge the mortgage debt, the expenses of the sale and the costs of the action, and which may be sold separately without material injury to the parties interested, be sold by or under the direction of the sheriff of the county, or a referee, and that the plaintiff, or any party, may become a purchaser on such sale; that the sheriff or referee execute a deed; that out of the proceeds of the sale, unless otherwise directed, he pay the expenses of the sale, and that he pay to the plaintiff, or his attorney, the amount of the debt, interest and costs, or so much as the purchase money will pay of the same and that he take the receipt of the plaintiff, or his attorney, for the amount so paid, and file the same with his report of sale, and that the purchaser be let into possession on production of the deed. See also C.P.A., § 1082. See C.P.A., § 1086 for provision of judgment where mortgage debt is not all due.

Blank spaces are left for the insertion of the name of the officer who is to conduct the sale, and also for the various amounts as taxed by the clerk.

§ 447. Service of Judgment of Foreclosure and Sale With Notice of Entry. 

The judgment of foreclosure and sale is served with notice of entry upon the attorneys for the parties who have appeared and not waived. A certified copy thereof is served upon the sheriff or referee as directed therein. 

Arrangement is made with such officer for the date of the sale. Arrangement is also made for the publication of the notice of sale as provided in C.P.A., § 986. 

S448. The Auctioneer.

Following a long established and well recognized practice in foreclosure actions in the First Department, the referee engages the services of an auctioneer to conduct a sale under his direction. Edbro Realty Co., Inc., v. Clarey, 141 Misc. 779, 253 N. Y. S. 282, aff'd 235 

A. D. 714. His fee for conducting the sale is fifteen dollars and is paid by the purchaser. He cannot receive directly or indirectly, any other fee for making the sale, except where the sale is made at a public sales room in which case he may demand and receive such further amount not exceeding five dollars for each parcel separately sold when he has actually paid for the privilege or right of making the sale in such sales room. 

N. Y. Cty. Supreme Court Special Term Rule XIV. 

The rule further provides that the auctioneer selected for the purpose must be one who is a duly licensed

$449 

real estate broker, or one who is a duly licensed real estate salesman and has had at the time of sale a real estate salesman's license for not less than five years, or one who has been regularly engaged in the sale of real estate at auction for not less than five years prior to 

January 1, 1934. See other local court rules. 

§ 449. Notice of Sale-Form. 

A notice of sale is prepared, signed by the referee or sheriff as the case may be and sent to the newspaper indicated in the judgment, for publication; or the advertisement may be handled through an advertisement agency. 

C.P.A., § 986 provides that notice of the sale must be given by the officer making it, as prescribed for the sale by a sheriff of real property by virtue of an execution, unless the property is situated wholly or partly in a city, or in an incorporated village of the first class in which a daily, semi-weekly or tri-weekly newspaper is published, and, in that case, by publishing notice of the sale in such a daily, semi-weekly or tri-weekly paper, at least twice in each week for three successive weeks, or in a weekly paper published in a city or in such incorporated village of the first class, once in each of the six weeks immediately preceding the sale, or in the counties of New York and Kings in two such daily papers. If the property is situated in a city, or a village of the first class, in which no newspaper is published daily, semi-weekly or tri-weekly, and there is an adjoining city, in the same or another county, in which a newspaper is published, such notice may be published either twice a week for three successive weeks immediately preceding the sale in a daily, semi-weekly or tri-weekly newspaper of the latter city or once a week for six successive weeks immediately preceding the sale in a weekly newspaper of such city. Notice of postponement

449 459 

of the sale must be published in the paper or papers wherein the notice of sale was published. 

The various local court rules should be consulted to learn what additions, if any, are required to be made to the usual notice of sale. For example, New York County 

Supreme Court, Special Term, Rule XIV provides that with the notice of sale, there shall be published a diagram of the property to be sold, showing the street or avenue where located, the street and avenue number, if any, and specifying the number of feet to the nearest cross street or avenue. Where the sale is made to satisfy any lien or charge on the property sold, the rule further provides that the approximate amount of such lien or charge shall be stated in a note annexed to such notice of sale, and where there are taxes and assessments or other liens upon the property, which are to be allowed to the purchaser out of the purchase money, or which are to be paid by the referee, the referee or officer making the sale shall also state in a note annexed to the notice of sale, the approximate amount of the charge or lien.

§ 452. Terms of Sale-Form. 

In preparation for the sale, the terms thereof are drawn; for they are required to be made known upon the sale in pursuance of C.P.A., § 986. The memorandum of sale, which appears thereon, is signed by the purchaser,. who is required to pay ten per cent of the purchase price at the time and place of the sale. If the plaintiff is the purchaser, the payment of ten per cent may be waived,. as indicated in the illustrated form.

The terms of sale may read as follows:

§ 453. The Sale-Duty of Referee. 

If the publication of the notice of sale is for three weeks, the sale takes place on any day on or after the twenty-first day and on or before the twenty-eighth day after the day of the first publication; and if the publication is for six weeks, the sale takes place on any day on or after the forty-second day and on or before the fortyninth day after the day of the first publication. The sale of the mortgaged premises must be made at public auction and to the highest bidder. C.P.A., § 986. The duties of the referee under the judgment are ministerial in their character. If he disregards the directions of the judgment, he does so at his peril. People ex rel. Day v. 

Bergen, 53 N. Y. 404; Heller v. Cohen, 154 N. Y. 299. 

§ 454. Closing-Referee's Report of Sale-Form. 

The referee's report and verification may be signed and the deed executed, upon the closing, upon payment 30

$ 454 

by the purchaser of the balance of the purchase price, unless the plaintiff is the purchaser, in which case a receipt therefor by the plaintiff or his attorney may be produced.. Receipts for all payments made as provided in the judgment are produced, to wit, receipted bills for advertisement expenses, taxes, assessments, water charges with interest and penalties thereon, and receipts for attorney's allowances, costs and disbursements, and for referee's and auctioneer's fees. 

Where the judgment directs the sale, the officer making it must pay out of the proceeds, unless the judgment otherwise directs, all taxes, assessments and water rates which are liens upon the property sold, and redeem the property sold from any sales for unpaid taxes, assessments or water rates which have not apparently become absolute. The sums necessary to make those payments and redemptions are deemed expenses of the sale within the meaning of that expression as used in Article 65. 

C.P.A., § 1087. To the same effect is Rule 259. Under this section, the referee appointed to make the sale has the duty, if so directed in the judgment, to ascertain and pay all taxes which are liens upon the property and to redeem the property, if sold, from any unpaid taxes, as already indicated. This being the case, the referee would be empowered, if in doubt as to the validity of any tax, to inquire into the same. Moreover, the purchaser has the burden of producing before the referee, proof of outstanding tax liens, and if the referee is in doubt as to the validity of any such lien, he may apply to the court for instructions. First Citizen's Bank & Trust Co. v. Rutger 

Devel. Corp., 144 Misc. 745; 259 N. Y. S. 370, citing People ex rel. Day v. Bergen, 53 N. Y. 404; Easton v. Pickersgill, 55 N. Y. 310.

The usual fee of one hundred dollars is paid to the referee, but, as the court in Ryan v. Majestic Home Builders, Inc., et al., 238 A. D. 167, 263 N. Y. S. 718, points out, the referee is not entitled to this sum if his fees and commissions, when computed in pursuance of C.P.A.,

454 465 

§ 1546, does not total that amount.

Railroad Co-Opera tive Building & Loan Ass'n v. Cautero et al., 240 A. D. 

318; 270 N. Y. S. 99.

A receipt for the referee's fee is obtained and, together with all other receipts, receipted bills and notice of sale with proof of publication, are annexed to the report of sale.

The report of sale may read as follows:

§ 455. Effect of Conveyance Upon Sale-Referee's Deed -Form. 

C.P.A., § 1085 provides that a conveyance upon a sale made pursuant to a final judgment in an action to foreclose a mortgage upon real property vests in the purchaser the same estate only that would have vested in the

8 455 

mortgagee if the equity of redemption had been foreclosed. Such a conveyance is as valid as if it were executed by the mortgagor and mortgagee, and except as provided in sections 1079a and 1086, is an entire bar against each of them and against each party to the action who was duly summoned and every person claiming from, through or under a party by title accruing after the filing of the notice of the pendency of the action. Sautter v. 

Frick, 229 A. D. 345; 242 N. Y. S. 369, citing Rector, etc., of Christ P. E. Church v. Mack, 93 N. Y. 488.

The referee's deed may be in the following form:

§ 456. Filing Report of Sale. 

Within thirty days after the sale is completed and the proper conveyance executed to the purchaser, unless the time is extended by court order, there must be filed with the clerk the report of the officer making the sale, under oath, of the disposition of the proceeds of the sale accompanied by the vouchers of the persons to whom payments were ordered to be made. C.P.A., § 1088. After the thirty day period, a referee becomes functus officio and has no legal authority to make an amended report. 

Blumberg v. Giorgio, 239 A. D. 779, 264 N. Y. S. 1. 

§ 457. Serving Notice of Filing of Referee's Report of 

Sale.

A notice of filing of the referee's report of sale and of a motion to confirm the report may be served upon those who have appeared in like manner as already described under a notice of filing of the referee's report on a reference to compute and a motion to confirm. 

§ 458. Order Confirming Referee's Report of Sale- 

Form.

The final step in the foreclosure action in so far as it affects the title to the mortgaged premises is the entry of the order confirming the sale.

A motion to confirm the report of sale may not be made within three months after the filing of the report, but

$ 458 

shall, in any event, be made not later than four months after the filing of the report, except that if there be no surplus moneys arising from the sale of the mortgaged premises, an application to confirm may be made at any time after the report shall have been filed eight days. C.P.A., & 1082. 

Where the parties have defaulted in appearing, the proposed order to confirm the report may be submitted to the clerk at special term in the part devoted to ex parte business, accompanied by an affidavit; or where the parties have appeared, their consent to the entry of the order may be obtained, thus avoiding the necessity of making a motion therefor. In addition, there may be annexed a county clerk's certificate showing that no objections have been filed.

The order may read as follows: 

PRESENT:

Brooklyn, City of New York, on the

§ 461. Surplus Moneys. 

JOHN N. HARMAN, County Clerk of Kings County. 

All surplus moneys arising from the sale of the mortgaged premises are required to be deposited by the officer, appointed to conduct the sale, within five days after the same are received and ascertainable, to the credit of the action in a bank or trust company named by the court in the final judgment unless otherwise directed. C.P.A., § 1082; see Rule 261. Persons claiming surplus money may, at any time before the confirmation of the report, file with the clerk in whose office the report is filed, a written notice of such claim, stating the nature and extent of the claim and the address of himself or his attorney. C.P.A., § 1082; Rule 262. See Wait's N. Y. 

Practice, Vol. 5 (4th Ed.), page 234. 

§ 462. Deficiency Judgment. 

A motion for leave to enter a deficiency judgment may be made simultaneously with the motion to confirm the report of sale, but in order that the title may be perfected without unnecessary delay, it is better practice to make a separate motion at a later time. Within ninety days after the consummation of the sale by delivery of the deed to the purchaser, a motion may be made on notice to those persons against whom a claim for deficiency is made. The matter is usually referred to a referee and the same procedure is followed as already described; to

$ 462 

wit, the entry of the order on the motion; the service of a certified copy of the order with notice of entry upon the referee named therein; the hearing; preparation of the referee's report; a motion to confirm the report; entry of an order confirming the report; and finally to have the clerk docket the judgment.

C.P.A., § 1083-a provides that upon such motion, the court, whether or not the respondent appears, shall determine, upon affidavit or otherwise as it shall direct, the fair and reasonable market value of the mortgaged premises as of the date such premises were bid in at auction or such nearest earlier date as there shall have been any market value thereof, and shall make an order directing the entry of a deficiency judgment. Such deficiency judgment shall be for an amount equal to the sum of the amount owing by the party liable as determined by the judgment with interest, plus the amount owing on all prior liens and encumbrances with interest, plus costs and disbursements of the action, including the referee's fee and disbursements, less the market value as determined by the court or the sale price of the property, whichever shall be higher. If no motion for a deficiency judgment is made, the proceeds of the sale, regardless of the amount, are deemed to be in full satisfaction of the mortgage debt, and no right to recover any deficiency in any action or proceeding shall exist.

§ 463. In General. 

518 Matrimonial actions are commenced, tried and judgment entered therein in like manner as in other civil actions. However, these actions are strictly statutory and care, therefore, should be taken in drawing the complaint to recite the jurisdictional requirements. Crouch v. 

Crouch, 193 A. D. 221, 183 N. Y. S. 657; Walter v. Walter, 217 N. Y. 439. They may be brought in the Supreme 

Court only. They include actions for divorce; actions for the dissolution of the marriage; actions for separation and actions for annulment. 

§ 464. Action for Divorce. 

There is only one ground for divorce in New York State; to wit, adultery of one of the parties. And where that exists, the husband or wife is entitled to maintain the action against the other party to the marriage divorcing the parties and dissolving the marriage by reason of the defendant's adultery, if the plaintiff can show the existence of any of the following jurisdictional require ments: (C.P.A., § 1147) 

1. That both parties were residents of the state when the offence was committed. 

2. That the parties were married within the state. 

3. That the plaintiff was a resident of the state when the offence was committed and is a resident thereof when the action is commenced. Jenkinson v. Jenkinson, 214 

A. D. 263, 212 N. Y. S. 155. 

4. That the offence was committed within the state and the injured party when the action was commenced is a resident of the state. Sattenstein v. Sattenstein, 243 A. D. 

61, 276 N. Y. S. 443.

466 477 

MATRIMONIAL ACTIONS. 

§ 465. The Summons. 

Assuming that a party comes within any one of the cases aforementioned, and possesses the necessary evidence to support the charge of adultery, the next step is to draw a summons. The form of summons used in 

Supreme Court actions as already described is used. 

If it is served alone, it contains the endorsement on the face thereof, "Action for Divorce". C.P.A., § 1167. 

§ 466. The Complaint in a Divorce Action-Form. 

If the summons is accompanied by a complaint, as it usually is, the latter will read as follows:

SUPREME COURT OF THE  County of New York. 

The plaintiff above named, by her attorney, Raymond Smith, complaining of the defendant, respectfully shows to this Court and alleges:

FIRST: That at all the times hereinafter mentioned, the plaintiff and defendant were and still are residents of the City, County and State of New York. 

SECOND: That on the 7th day of April, 1931, in the Borough of Manhattan, City and State of New York, the plaintiff and defendant were intermarried. 

THIRD: That there is no issue of the said marriage. 

FOURTH: That on or about the 11th day of June, 1935, at 

117 Fifth Avenue, Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, the defendant committed adultery with a woman whose identity is unknown to the plaintiff.

FIFTH: That on or about the 14th day of June, 1935, at a

8 467 

hotel known as the Grand Hotel in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, the defendant committed adultery with a woman whose identity is unknown to the plaintiff. 

SIXTH That such acts of adultery were committed by the defendant without the consent, connivance, privity or procurement of the plaintiff.

SEVENTH: That five years have not elapsed since the discovery by the plaintiff of the commission of the said acts of adultery or any of them, and that the plaintiff has not voluntarily cohabited with the said defendant since the commission of any of the acts of adultery aforementioned and the discovery thereof by the plaintiff, nor has the plaintiff forgiven or condoned the same. 

EIGHTH That no decree of divorce has been obtained by the plaintiff or the defendant against each other in any court of this state or any other state or in any foreign country or dominion.

WHEREFORE, the plaintiff demands judgment against the defendant dissolving the bonds of matrimony between the plaintiff and the defendant and for such other, further and different relief as to the Court may seem just and proper in the premises. 

RAYMOND SMITH, 

Attorney for Plaintiff,

Office & Post Office Address, 

117 Broadway,

Borough of Manhattan, City of New York. 

§ 467. Service of Summons and Complaint. 

The summons and complaint are served personally upon the defendant by a process server, who must be certain of the identity of the defendant. He may be furnished with a photograph of the defendant, or, if possible, he may be accompanied by a person who is acquainted with the defendant, when effecting service. The affidavit of service follows the form previously described. 

At the time the summons and complaint are served upon the defendant, there may also be served motion papers for alimony and counsel fees.

$479 

MATRIMONIAL ACTIONS. 

§ 468. The Answer in a Divorce Action. 

The answer to the complaint in a divorce action is in the usual form. It need not, however, be verified, notwithstanding the fact that the complaint is verified. But where the answer contains a counterclaim setting up adultery, it must be verified with respect to such counterclaim if the complaint is verified. C.P.A., § 1148. See also Wait's New York Practice, Vol. 5 (4th Ed.), p. 425. 

§ 469. Jury Trial. 

Although jury trials are not frequent, nevertheless where an answer puts in issue the allegation of adultery, the court may of its own motion, and must on the application of either party, make an order directing the trial by a jury of that issue. And for this purpose the questions to be tried are prepared and settled. C.P.A., § 1149. See 

Wait's New York Practice, Vol. 5 (4th Ed.), p. 428. 

§ 470. Default in Answering-Uncontested Divorce. 

If the defendant fails to serve an answer, the plaintiff must nevertheless proceed in open court with the trial, since judgment cannot be entered upon default. C.P.R. 

283. This is known as an uncontested divorce. And this, rather than a contested divorce, is most frequent. But where the plaintiff wife demands alimony and the defendant does not interpose an answer, his attorney may nevertheless serve a notice of appearance upon the plaintiff's attorney, so that he may appear on the trial of the action and submit evidence which will aid the court in determining the reasonable amount of alimony to be awarded to the wife and which will not be beyond his ability to pay. 

§ 471. Noticing Case for Trial-In General. 

If the defendant intends to contest the action, it will be noticed for trial in the same manner as any other civil action. And if an order has been made in the action, granting or denying temporary alimony, the action will 31

8 473 

be entitled to a preference under subdivision 18 of section 

138 of the Civil Practice Act. But a preference will not be granted where the husband has defaulted in payment of alimony and counsel fees. Fennessy v. Fennessy, 111 

A. D. 181, 97 N. Y. S. 602. If it is to be an uncontested action, the plaintiff's attorney proceeds to place the case upon the calendar for trial by preparing a note of issue and an affidavit of regularity. 

§ 472. Note of Issue. 

The note of issue is in the usual form except that it is returnable in Special Term, Part III, in New York County, instead of the Trial Term part. In Bronx 

County, it is returnable in Special Term, Part I, and in 

Kings County in Special Term, Part V. If there has been an appearance, a copy of the note of issue may be served upon the defendant's attorney, otherwise this is not necessary. The original is filed with the County Clerk of 

New York County and a duplicate original is filed with the clerk of Special Term, Part III. In the other coun ties, the note of issue is filed with the clerk of the part wherein it is made returnable as already indicated. At the time of filing, a fee of twenty-six dollars is paid. This consists of twenty dollars for filing the note of issue, five dollars trial fee and one dollar for entering judgment. 

§ 473. Affidavit of Regularity-Form. 

An affidavit showing the default of the defendant accompanies the note of issue and reads as follows:

SUPREME COURT OF THE  County of New York. 

MARY ROE, Plaintiff. -against-

474 481

Bronx County follows the practice of New York County. 

In Kings County, however, uncontested divorce cases are not referred to official referees but are tried before the judge sitting in Special Term, Part V. 

§ 475. The Trial. 

Despite the fact that no answer has been served by the defendant, the plaintiff must nevertheless satisfactorily prove the allegations of his complaint and also by his own testimony or otherwise, that there is no judgment or decree of any court of the state of competent jurisdiction against him in favor of the defendant for a divorce on the ground of adultery. C.P.A., § 1150. And though the plaintiff establish the charge of adultery, he will not be entitled to a decree where he has not shown that the offence was not committed by procurement or connivance; that the offence was not forgiven; that the action was commenced within five years after the discovery thereof, and that the plaintiff is not guilty of adultery under such circumstances as to entitle the defendant to a divorce. 

C.P.A., § 1153. 

§ 476. Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law-Form. 

After the trial, a copy of the testimony is procured from the court stenographer. The original is filed. C.P. 

R. 282. The copy is used to prepare findings of fact and conclusions of law which are submitted for signature either to the judge, referee or official referee, depending on which one of these presided upon the trial. The proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law, making whatever slight changes are necessary to conform with local court rules, may read as follows:

$ 485 

MATRIMONIAL ACTIONS. 

SUPREME COURT OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK New York County. 

To the Supreme Court of the State of New York: 

The above cause having been duly brought on for trial at Special Term, Part III of this Court, before Mr. Justice Levy, one of the Justices thereof, on the 21st day of November, 1935, and the Court having by its order of reference referred the cause to the undersigned as official referee, and the plaintiff by her attorney having appeared and presented her verified complaint, written and oral proof of service of the summons and complaint on the defendant, affidavit of regularity of this proceeding, and the defendant, not having interposed an answer but having appeared by Matthew Lane, his attorney, and testimony having been heard in open court on the 23rd day of November, 1935, and due deliberation having been had, I decide and find as 

FINDINGS OF FACT 

I. The plaintiff now is and since April 7, 1931, has been a resident of the City, County and State of New York.

II. The plaintiff and defendant intermarried on the 7th day of April, 1931, in the Borough of Manhattan, City and State of 

New York. 

III. There is no issue of the said marriage.

IV. At 117 Fifth Avenue, Borough of Manhattan, City of 

New York, on or about the 11th day of June, 1935, and at the 

Grand Hotel, Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, on or about the 14th day of June, 1935, the defendant committed adultery with a woman whose identity is unknown to the plaintiff.

S 477 

V. That said acts of adultery were committed by the defendant without the consent, connivance, privity or procurement of the plaintiff.

VI. That five years have not elapsed since the discovery by the plaintiff of the commission of the said acts of adultery, and the plaintiff has not voluntarily cohabited with the defendant since the commission and discovery thereof, and she has not forgiven or condoned the same.

VII. There is no judgment of divorce between the plaintiff and the defendant in any court of this state or any other state or in any foreign country or dominion. 

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW 

I. The plaintiff is entitled to an interlocutory judgment dissolving the marriage between the plaintiff and the defendant and providing that unless for sufficient cause the court in the meantime shall have otherwise ordered, the said interlocutory judgment shall become the final judgment as of course three months after the entry and filing thereof because of the adultery of the defendant.

Dated: New York, November 25, 1935. 

JOHN FORD, Referee. 

§ 477. Motion to Confirm Referee's Report-Form. 

As soon as the findings are signed, a motion is made to confirm the referee's report. This is done by filing a notice of motion only, unaccompanied by any affidavit, with the clerk at Special Term. In New York County, the notice of motion is filed with the clerk of Special Term, Part III, two days before the return day. The motion is made returnable on a Friday of any week. N. Y. Cty. 

Supreme Ct. Spec. Term Rule III, subd. 10. This may vary in the other counties. On the return day the proposed interlocutory judgment is submitted and all the papers that were filed in the action are ordered sent up to the Clerk of Special Term, Part III. If there has been an appearance, a copy of the notice of motion, together

MATRIMONIAL ACTIONS. 

with findings of fact and conclusions of law with notice of entry, may be served upon the plaintiff's attorney. 

The notice of motion reads as follows:

§ 478. Interlocutory Judgment—Form. 

A motion to confirm the report of a referee is invariably granted. It is necessary, however, to file the decision

8 478 

of the court or the report of the referee and enter the interlocutory judgment thereon within fifteen days after the party becomes entitled to file or enter the same, otherwise a court order must be obtained and sufficient cause shown for the delay in order to entitle the party to file the report or enter the judgment after the expiration of that period of time. C.P.A., § 1175. The proposed interlocutory judgment is submitted on the return day of the motion to confirm the referee's report. The decision will be to the effect that the motion is granted and that the interlocutory judgment of divorce is signed. A note of the date of such signing is made in the litigation register. 

A diary entry is made three months hence as the day on which the plaintiff will become entitled to a final decree. 

A printed form of the interlocutory judgment may be obtained from the Clerk of Special Term. It may, wherever the circumstances require, contain provisions for the payment of alimony and for the support and custody of minor children.

An interlocutory judgment reads as follows: 

PRESENT: 

At a Special Term, Part III, of the Supreme 

Court of the State of New York held in and for the  at the County Courthouse thereof, in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, on the 1st day of November, 1930.

HON. ALFRED H. TOWNLEY, Justice.

§ 479. Final Decree of Divorce-Form. 

At the expiration of the three month period, a motion is made for final judgment. See Wait's N. Y. Practice, Vol. 5 (4th Ed.), page 438. In New York County and such other counties where the interlocutory judgment becomes final at the expiration of three months without application to the court, the clerk signs a certificate which has been prepared and annexed to the interlocutory judgment by the plaintiff's attorney to the effect that no order

§ 491. 

MATRIMONIAL ACTIONS. 

has been filed since the entry of the interlocutory judg ment. The certificate reads as follows: 

CERTIFICATE OF COUNTY CLERK, COUNTY CLERK'S OFFICE. 

I HEREBY CERTIFY that a decision and an interlocutory judgment of divorce in favor of MARY ROE in an action brought in the Supreme Court by MARY ROE, plaintiff, against RICHARD ROE, defendant, was entered in this office on the 25th day of November, 1930, and that no order has been filed in this action since the entry of the interlocutory judgment. 

Dated, New York, February 25, 1930.

DANIEL E. FINN, Clerk.

The interlocutory judgment to which is annexed the foregoing certificate constitutes the final decree. If the decree provides for the payment of alimony, a certified copy thereof is required to be served upon the defendant personally so that the basis may be laid for contempt proceedings if the defendant fails to comply with the judgment. A copy of the decree is submitted to the clerk, who certifies it upon payment of a small fee. 

§ 480. Action for Separation. 

A husband or wife may maintain an action against the other for a decree of separation for either of the follow ing causes: (C.P.A., § 1161). 

1. Cruel and inhuman treatment of the plaintiff by the defendant. 

2. Such conduct on the part of the defendant towards the plaintiff as may render it unsafe and improper for the latter to cohabit with the former. 

3. The abandonment of the plaintiff by the defendant. 

4. Where the wife is the plaintiff, the neglect or refusal of the defendant to provide for her. 

In this connection it is interesting to note that the

$ 480 

strictness of the ancient rule which limits cruelty in matrimonial actions to violence or threats of violence has been relaxed. Thus the plaintiff may now show such conduct which, though not amounting to physical violence or apprehension thereof, nevertheless causes a state of mind in the plaintiff rendering the continuation of the marital relation so reasonably intolerable as to constitute cruel and inhuman treatment. Heylmun v. Heylmun, 119 Misc. 

113, 195 N. Y. S. 335. A Court of Appeals decision which is quoted very frequently warns that the test of cruel and inhuman treatment, where no blows are struck or threatened, should be applied with great caution; that insulting and angry words may cause discomfort, but they amount to incompatibility of temper, which is not a ground for separation in New York State. Pearson v. Pearson, 230

N. Y. 141. The court in this case stated that because the plaintiff was a physician, his wife's jealousy of his women patients and her nagging charges of his misconduct with them made in the presence of others might conceivably so interfere with the practice of his profession as to impair his health and that such conduct would constitute cruel and inhuman treatment. In the Heylmun case, the court held that although the individual acts complained of would not be sufficient ground for separation, nevertheless all the acts taken together would constitute such ground. These acts consisted of the defendant's sullen and morose attitude toward his wife, permitting the house to remain out of repair and examining the potato and squash parings to see if the wife were wasteful. 

An abandonment which entitles a party to a decree of separation must be one which contemplates a voluntary separation of one party from the other without justification and with the intention of not returning. Williams v. 

Williams, 130 N. Y. 193. See also Wait's N. Y. Practice, Vol. 5 (4th Ed.), page 448.

Assuming that grounds exist for the maintenance of

481 493: 

MATRIMONIAL ACTIONS. 

the action, the plaintiff must also show the existence of any of the following jurisdictional requirements: 

1. Both parties are residents of the state when the action is commenced. 

2. The parties were married within the state and the plaintiff is a resident thereof when the action is commenced. 

3. The parties having been married without the state, have become residents of the state, and have continued to be residents thereof at least one year; and the plaintiff was a resident when the action was commenced. C.P.A., 

§ 1162. 

§ 481. Existence of Valid Separation Agreement as Bar to Separation Action. 

Assuming that the plaintiff has ground for separation and comes within one of the cases mentioned in Section 1162 of the Civil Practice Act, nevertheless, before commencing action, it is advisable to inquire whether the. parties have signed a separation agreement. If there is a valid and subsisting agreement, the action cannot be maintained for the following reasons:

If cruelty is the ground for the maintenance of the action, an examination of the facts may, in all probability, show that the acts of cruelty existed prior to the date of the separation agreement. Under such circumstances, the courts hold that by entering into the agreement, the differences which existed between the parties and thegrounds otherwise available became adjusted and composed by the agreement with the same result as if a judgment of the court had been granted, and the plaintiff is therefore bound by the agreement. In other words, before the agreement was entered into, the plaintiff had sufficient ground to entitle her to a decree, but since she did not choose to seek the aid of the court, but rather tosettle her differences by agreement, that agreement was equivalent to a judgment of the court decreeing a separa--

$ 482 

tion and the plaintiff is bound thereby. 

Benesch, 182 A. D. 221, 169 N. Y. S. 561.

Benesch v. 

Again, if abandonment is the ground alleged for the maintenance of the action, the separation agreement again constitutes a bar. The courts hold that the question of abandonment cannot arise after the execution of a separation agreement by reason of the fact that when the parties enter into a separation agreement, they agree to live separate and apart, and consequently the separation is with the consent of the plaintiff and in accordance with her wishes, and therefore there can be no abandonment under the circumstances. Haskell v. Haskell, 33 A. D. 

126, 53 N. Y. S. 346.

And as long as that agreement remains a valid and subsisting one, it is binding upon the parties. The wife cannot ignore the agreement. If she must sue for separation, her remedy is to first sue in equity to set the agreement aside for fraud, undue influence or any other ground upon which a contract may be set aside. It may not be necessary for her to do this, however, if the husband breaches the agreement and, for example, refuses to provide for her in pursuance of the contract. In that event, the wife may elect to abandon the agreement and bring suit for separation. Winter v. Winter, 191 N. Y. 

462; Randolph v. Field, 165 A. D. 279, 150 N. Y. S. 822.

And in such event, also, the wife may make application for alimony and counsel fees.

Where the parties have separated and wish to settle their differences by agreement, rather than enlist the aid of the court, they may enter into an agreement reading

WHEREAS, differences have arisen between the parties as a result of which they have separated and are now living separate and apart and intend to continue to live separate and apart; and 

WHEREAS, without in any way acknowledging upon whom is the fault or condoning the conduct of the one or the other which has led to the existing state of affairs, the Husband and Wife and each of them desire by means of this agreement to adjust their respective property rights and to provide for the support and maintenance of the Wife;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the sum of One ($1.00) Dollar, by each of the parties to the other in hand paid, the receipt whereof is hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto hereby agree as follows: 

FIRST: The parties hereto do hereby mutually agree to continue to live separate and apart from each other and each shall have the right to do so free from any marital control, authority, restraint, interference or molestation, directly or indirectly, by the other, as though they were unmarried.

The Husband agrees to permit the

to the Wife the sum of $150 each and every week during said period. d) Commencing October 1st, 1935, and continuing during the lifetime of the Wife or until her remarriage, the Husband agrees to pay to the Wife the sum of $200 each and every week.

§ 483. The Complaint in a Separation Action—Form. 

An action for separation is commenced in the usual manner by the service of a summons, which, if served alone, must contain the endorsement on the face thereof, 

"Action for Separation". C.P.A., § 1167. In drawing the complaint, care should be taken to note Rule 280 of the Rules of Civil Practice, which provides that a complaint in an action for separation must specify particularly the nature and circumstances of the defendant's misconduct and set forth the time and place of each act complained of with reasonable certainty. The courts indicate how far they will go in requiring such specific facts and circumstances together with dates pursuant to this rule. In the case of Rebstock v. Rebstock, 144 N. Y. 

S. 289, for example, the complaint alleged that on one occasion, in their home, the defendant threw a knife across the table at the plaintiff. The court held the allegation insufficient because it did not fully disclose when it happened or what the nature and circumstances were. 

The complaint further alleged that on a certain day, the plaintiff came home and found the defendant in the kitchen and that she took a frying pan and threw it at him, hitting him on the shoulder. The court held this allegation insufficient because there was no allegation that the plaintiff was injured or that he felt any fear of injury, or that his clothes were injured; and further that the plaintiff might have induced the assault or it may have been done merely in fun. 

A complaint in a separation action may read as follows:

MARY ROE, 

-against- Plaintiff,

The plaintiff above-named, by her attorney, Raymond Smith, complaining of the defendant, respectfully shows to this Court and alleges:

SECOND: That there is no issue of the said marriage.

THIRD: That since the marriage of the plaintiff and the defendant, the defendant's conduct toward the plaintiff has been cruel and abusive in that the defendant drank to excess, neglected the plaintiff and consorted with women of ill-repute. (Specify in detail the acts constituting cruelty such as the following allegations :)

Both the defendant and his companion were intoxicated and in an hilarious mood. The plaintiff and defendant quarrelled by reason of the presence of the said Jane Doe, whereupon the defendant drew a revolver, loaded it, and threatened the plaintiff's life. The plaintiff was obliged to take refuge in her room, which she locked and remained therein for the remainder of the afternoon and the evening in fear.

(Specify further acts and if the complaint, in addition to the ground of cruelty, is to be based upon charges of abandonment and neglect to provide, the following allegations may be added:)

§ 484. Defense in a Separation Action. 

The defendant in an action for separation may set up in justification, the misconduct of the plaintiff; and if that defense is established to the satisfaction of the court, the defendant is entitled to judgment. C.P.A., § 1163. 

See Wait's N. Y. Practice, Vol. 5 (4th Ed.), page 453. 

§ 485. Procedure in Separation Action Following Service of Summons. 

A separation action is noticed for trial and the subsequent steps are taken in the same manner as described under an action for divorce, except that no interlocutory judgment is entered. This action is likewise entitled to a preference under subdivision 18 of section 138 of the Civil Practice Act, if an order has been made therein, granting or denying temporary alimony. The final judgment is entered after the findings of fact and conclusions of law have been signed. The judgment may separate the parties forever or for a limited time. C.P.A., § 1161. 

§ 486. Judgment of Separation-Form. 

A certified copy of the final judgment in an action for separation with notice of entry thereof is required to be served upon the defendant personally if it contains a provision for the payment of alimony.
