§ 653. Commissions of Executor. 

On the settlement of the account, the surrogate must allow to the executor, administrator, guardian or testamentary trustee all just, reasonable and necessary expenses which have been paid by him. If such representative is an attorney, compensation for legal services such as is just and reasonable is allowed. In addition to the expenses, any one of the foregoing receives compensation as follows: 

For receiving and paying all sums not exceeding two thousand dollars, at the rate of five per centum; on sums not amounting to more than twenty thousand dollars, at the rate of two and one-half per centum; on sums not exceeding twenty-eight thousand dollars, at the rate of one and one-half per centum; and on sums above fifty thousand dollars, at the rate of two per centum. Surr. 

Ct. Act, § 285. See further provisions as to compensation in said section. 

§ 654. Accounting-Judicial Settlement. 

When the time stated in the published notice to present claims has expired or if no notice has been published, then after the expiration of seven months since the issuance of letters, the executor may present to the surrogate's court his account and a petition praying

$ 655 

that his account may be judicially settled and that all necessary and proper parties may be cited to show cause why such settlement should not be had. Surr. Ct. 

Act, § 261. 

Where he does not do so voluntarily an executor may be compelled to account where fifteen days have elapsed after the expiration of the time stated in the published notice for the presentation of claims or seven months have elapsed from the issuance of letters or where letters issued to him have been revoked, or for any other reason, his powers have ceased. Surr. Ct. Act, § 258. See also Wait's N. Y. Practice, Vol. 7 [4th Ed.], 778.

A surrogate, in a proceeding before him, having for its object the settlement of an account and obtaining a decree for distribution of funds, when all parties are present, has authority to construe the will, determine the meaning and validity wherever necessary to make his decree. Garlock v. Vandervort, 128 N. Y. 374. 

§ 655. Release and Discharge of Executor-Form. 

Where an account has been judicially settled, and any part of the estate or fund remains and is ready to be distributed, the decree directs payment thereof to the persons entitled thereto. Surr. Ct. Act, § 267. But the legatees may waive a judicial accounting of the estate and the issuance of a citation therefor. 

A release and discharge of the executor should be drawn and executed before final distribution is made and may read as follows:

In the Matter of the Estate of 

JOHN DOE,

P. 463-1933. 

Release and Discharge of Executrix. 

Deceased.

§ 656. Consent of Substitution of Attorney—Form. 

PAGE 663 664 665 666 A party to an action has an absolute right to discharge his attorney with or without cause. The attorney so discharged, however, is entitled to a lien for the services already rendered. Robinson v. Rogers, 237 N. Y. 467.

Where another attorney is to be substituted for the discharged attorney, a consent to the substitution of the attorneys in the form of a stipulation is prepared and signed by the attorney of record and both signed and acknowledged by the party who requests the substitution. It is filed with the clerk of the court in which the action or proceeding is pending. The making and filing of such a substitution has the same effect as an order of substitution. An attorney may also be changed by order.

C.P.R. 56. 

A consent to the substitution reads as follows: 

JOHN DOE, Plaintiff, —against— 

 663

$ 657 

IT IS HEREBY STIPULATED AND CONSENTED that Richard Jones, Esq., of No. 100 Broadway, Borough of Manhattan, City of 

New York, be and he hereby is substituted in place and stead of Robert Smith as attorney for the defendant in the above entitled action and that this substitution be entered into effect without further notice.

RICHARD ROE, ROBERT SMITH. 

  SS.: 

On the 10th day of March, 1936, before me personally came

RICHARD ROE, to me known and known to me to be the individual described in, and who executed, the foregoing consent and acknowledged to me that he executed the same. 

MARY JONES, Notary Public-New York County. 

§ 657. Assignment-Form. 

If the claim is one which is assignable, it is customary for a non-resident to assign his claim to a resident for the purpose of bringing suit thereon. This obviates the necessity of filing a bond as security for costs. 

The assignment should be acknowledged, care being taken to follow the form of acknowledgment used in the foreign state of the residence of the assignor. The county clerk's certificate of such state should be subjoined to the acknowledgment. 

The assignment may be prepared and forwarded to the non-resident and when received, duly signed and acknowledged, suit is commenced thereon. 

The assignment may read as follows: 

KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS: 

I, John Doe, in consideration of the sum of One ($1.00)

Dollar, lawful money of the United States, to me in hand paid before the sealing and delivery of these presents, receipt whereof

$ 665 

MISCELLANEOUS. 

is hereby acknowledged, and other good and valuable considerations, have sold, assigned, transferred and set over, and by these presents do sell, assign, transfer and set over unto Richard Roe of the City of New York, his executors, administrators and assigns, to his and their own proper use and benefit, my certain claim against Bowman Co., Inc., of 200 West 23rd 

Street, Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, in the sum of $5,215, for damages arising out of breach of contract of employment; 

Giving and granting unto the said Richard Roe, his executors, administrators and assigns, full power and authority for his and their own use and benefit, but at his or their own cost, to ask, demand, collect, receive, compound and give good acquittance for the same, or any part thereof, in the name of the undersigned, or otherwise to prosecute or withdraw any suits or proceedings at law or in equity therefor. 

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand and seal this 11th day of February, 1936.

In Presence of: 

ELINOR SMITH. 

STATE OF NEW JERSEY,

ELINOR SMITH, Notary Public of New Jersey. 

§ 658. Retainer Agreement Form. 

It is customary for attorneys to have written retainer agreements in order that there may be no misunderstanding as to the terms whereby an attorney is

$ 659 

employed to prosecute a suit. An agreement of this sort, may read as follows: 

Messrs. Wright & Hughes, 100 Broadway, New York, N. Y.

Gentlemen: 

January 12, 1935.

The undersigned hereby retains you as his attorneys to prosecute his claim against "The New York Evening Journal" by reason of the fact that "The New York Evening Journal" did falsely, wickedly, maliciously, intentionally and wilfully print and publish a false scandalous and defamatory article of and concerning the undersigned in the newspaper called "The New York Evening Journal", and to represent him in any action brought for that purpose and hereby agrees to pay you thirtythree and one-third (33 1/3%) per cent of any recovery obtained herein as the result of an action or compromise, settlement or otherwise.

The undersigned further agrees to pay you Two Hundred and Fifty ($250) Dollars as retainer upon the signing of this agreement, Fifty ($50) Dollars of which is to be used in the payment of disbursements.

The undersigned further agrees to pay all disbursements in excess of Fifty ($50) Dollars entailed through the institution of suit or otherwise in connection with the said claim. 

Very truly yours,

ACCEPTED: 

JOHN DOE. 

§ 659. Filing Retainer Agreement in Personal Injury Actions-Form. 

In the ordinary case, it is not necessary to file a retainer agreement but in personal injury actions, a record thereof is required to be filed in the Appellate 

Division. Rule 4a of the Special Rules Regulating the Conduct of Attorneys and Counsellors-at-Law in the

$ 667 

MISCELLANEOUS. 

First Judicial Department. See local department rules. 

The rule provides, in substance, that in claims or actions for damages for personal injuries or for death or loss of services, resulting from personal injuries, an attorney who enters into an agreement whereby his compensation for services rendered or to be rendered in connection with such claim or action is contingent upon the successful prosecution or settlement thereof shall, within ten days from the date of such retainer or agreement of compensation, sign and file in the office of the 

Clerk of the Appellate Division, First Judicial Depart ment, a written statement setting forth the date of such retainer or agreement of compensation, the name and address of the client and of the attorney, the date and place of the occurrence of the personal injury and the terms of the compensation.

The rule provides that no attorney shall accept or act under any such retainer or agreement for compensation in which the name of the attorney is left blank at the time of the execution.

The statement may read as follows: 

SUPREME COURT OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK Appellate Division-First Judicial Department. 

JOHN DOE,

RICHARD ROE, Plaintiff, —against— Defendant. 

Oral retainer September 10, 1935. 

Client: John Doe, residing at 34 East 50th Street, New 

York City. 

Plaintiff's attorneys: Wright & Hughes, 100 Broadway, New 

York City.

$659 

Action for damages resulting from injuries sustained as a result of the defendant negligently operating his automobile at the northeast corner of 50th St. and Madison Avenue, New York City, on September 5, 1935. 

Client agrees to pay his attorneys 33 1/3 % of any recovery obtained as the result of an action or through compromise, settlement or otherwise, and further agrees to pay all costs and disbursements necessarily incurred in his behalf in the prosecution of his claim.
